title: Entire minimal-graph Bernstein problem
statement: For which dimensions \(m\) must every smooth entire solution \(u:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\) of the minimal-surface equation be affine?
status: As of November 2026: resolved. Every such graph is affine for \(m\leq7\); non-affine entire graphs exist for \(m\geq8\). The counterexamples were published in 1969 by \citet{bombieridegiorgigiusti1969minimal}. The later Russian translation is not the result\textquotesingle s discovery date.

title: Irreducible representations of an interval current group
statement: After fixing the regularity and topology of a group of maps \([0,1]\to SU(2)\), classify its continuous irreducible unitary representations up to equivalence. Distinguish operator-norm continuity from strong continuity; the notebook specifies neither the map category nor this convention.
status: As of November 2026: partly developed, with an archival ambiguity. In the smooth compact-semisimple setting, norm-continuous irreducibles are finite evaluation tensors \citep[Theorem 4.11; group theorem 4.15 in the arXiv version]{janssensneeb2015norm}; preprint 2013, online 2014, print 2015. Positive-energy and measurable-current results impose other hypotheses \citep{janssensneeb2024positive,araki1970factorizable}. The checked literature does not supply a full strong-continuity classification for every interpretation of the notebook.

title: Interval support of an irreducible current-group representation
statement: In a specified continuous unitary representation category for \(SU(2)\)-valued interval currents, does there exist an irreducible representation nontrivial on currents supported in every nonempty open subinterval? Equivalently in the full-support case, no proper closed subset carries the representation in the sense recorded on P000291.
status: As of November 2026: the chapter proves existence for strong continuity on \(C^1([0,1],SU(2))\), with irreducibility also on the smooth subgroup and full interval support. This constructed representation has no strongly continuous uniform-topology extension. Smooth norm-continuous irreducibles instead have finite support \citep{janssensneeb2015norm}. The high-dimensional energy theorem does not apply to an interval, whose energy representation is reducible \citep{ismagilov1976unitary,ismagilov1981segment}. These are precise positive and negative variants; the unrecorded archival category and broader classification remain unresolved here. No historical novelty is claimed for the construction.

title: Analytic approximation of formal solutions
statement: Given analytic equations \(F(x,y)=0\) over \(\mathbb C\) and a formal solution \(\widehat y(x)\) with the prescribed constant term, does every finite jet of \(\widehat y\) extend to a convergent solution of the same equations?
status: As of November 2026: resolved affirmatively by \citet{artin1968analytic}, published December 1968. For every \(c\), a convergent solution can be chosen congruent to \(\widehat y\) modulo \((x)^c\). Raynaud presented the result at Bourbaki in June 1969; that exposition appeared in 1971 \citep[Theorem 1]{raynaud1969artin}. The given formal series itself need not converge.

title: Rota's finite-field vector-space Ramsey conjecture
statement: For fixed \(q,r,\ell,k\), \(1\leq\ell<k\), does every \(r\)-coloring of the \(\ell\)-subspaces of a sufficiently large \(F_q^N\) admit a \(k\)-subspace monochromatic in dimension \(\ell\)?
status: Solved by the Graham--Leeb--Rothschild theorem; January 1972 announcement. No identical earlier problem was found in the supplied previous index.

title: Quadratic pairs in characteristic three
statement: Classify nontrivial finite groups \(G\) and faithful irreducible \(F_3G\)-modules generated by elements acting with \((g-I)^2=0\).
status: Later classification work includes Chermak's 2002 preprint/2004 article, Theorems A--B, for the component case, together with its cited component-free treatment. The notebook's separate characteristic-two slogan has insufficient restrictions for the same identification.

title: Factor criteria for infinite quantum spin states
statement: When does a state of the spin UHF algebra have a factor GNS representation, and which types can occur?
status: Powers\' 1967 relative-commutant correlation criterion answers the factor question; product states and Araki's one-dimensional finite-range Gibbs states supply established families. The type depends on the state. No identical spin-chain problem was found in the supplied previous index.

title: Elementary proof of the four-subspace deformation example
statement: Give a direct proof that \(S(5,2)\oplus S(1,2)\) has arbitrarily small deformations of type \(S(3,2)\oplus S(3,2)\), although the two individual summands are rigid.
status: The normal forms are identified in the 1971 classification. The requested deformation over \(\mathbf C\) is proved in Section~\ref{dev:four-subspaces} by the dense open orbit of \(S(3,2)^{\oplus2}\); an analytic one-parameter family follows in a Grassmann chart. The exact historical publication of the elementary proof was not verified. No mathematical openness is claimed.

title: The unit-sheaf cohomology of the punctured elliptic curve
status: Solved by the Picard group of a smooth elliptic curve with its point at infinity removed.

title: Punctured affine cohomology and residue duality
statement: Compute \(H^*(\mathbf A^n\setminus\{0\},\mathcal O)\) and identify the module and residue pairing in its top nonzero degree.
status: Solved classical localization/Koszul calculation. For \(n\geq2\) the top group is the module of Laurent monomials negative in every variable; its residue dual is restricted linear, not ring-linear. Earlier affine-cover and non-affineness entries 1965-70.6 and 1965-58.7 are related background, not an identical unresolved question.

title: Homotoping a distribution to a foliation
statement: Is every smooth constant-rank subbundle of a tangent bundle homotopic through subbundles to the tangent distribution of a nonsingular foliation?
status: Negative in general, as reported from Bott's pre-seminar integrability obstruction. Normal Pontryagin-ring classes in degrees above twice the codimension obstruct such a homotopy. The compressed CP² example is not securely identified and is not needed to state the obstruction. Earlier item 1968-149.3 records a related foliation-existence slogan, but its class-F title alone does not establish identical quantifiers and no earlier problem ID is supplied; the link is thematic.

title: Analytic and combinatorial torsion
statement: Equality of Ray--Singer and Reidemeister torsion for closed manifolds with an acyclic unitary flat bundle, with the determinant-line interpretation when cohomology is present.
status: As of November 2026, solved: Cheeger\textquoteright s 1977 announcement and M\"uller\textquoteright s 1978 proof establish the unitary comparison. The 1971 report is a preprint occurrence, not its solution.

title: Gudkov congruence for maximal real plane curves
statement: For every nonsingular real projective \(M\)-curve of degree \(2k\), prove \(p-m\equiv k^2\pmod8\), with \(p,m\) the even/odd nesting counts.
status: As of November 2026, solved by Rokhlin: note received 29 December 1971, published 1972. Arnold\textquoteright s modulo-four result was the March 1971 intermediate step.

title: A bounded linear operator with a dense orbit
statement: Does there exist a separable infinite-dimensional Banach space and a bounded linear operator on it with an orbit dense in the entire space? The notebook realizes this on sequence spaces by \(\lambda S\), \(|\lambda|>1\).
status: As of November 2026, the sequence-space existence question was already answered by Rolewicz in 1969. No universal assertion about all nonseparable or finite-dimensional spaces is included.

title: Modular parametrization of a rational elliptic curve
statement: For every elliptic curve \(E/\mathbb Q\) of conductor \(N\), construct a nonconstant morphism \(X_0(N)\to E\) over \(\mathbb Q\), equivalently identify its \(L\)-series with a weight-two newform.
status: As of November 2026, solved: the full modularity theorem was proved by Breuil, Conrad, Diamond, and Taylor and published in 2001.

title: Which sequences of coherent states are complete?
statement: Characterize sets \(\Lambda\subset\mathbb C\) for which the normalized coherent states span the Bargmann--Fock space densely, equivalently its uniqueness sets.
status: As of November 2026, Perelomov\textquoteright s lattice criterion and the stated Mitkovski--Wick perturbation criteria are verified. An unrestricted characterization is not established by this audit; a September 2026 zero-set preprint remains an unverified lead. Sampling density theorems alone do not answer the exact question.

title: Uniform centered uncertainty for an orthonormal basis
statement: Does \(L^2(\mathbb R)\) admit an orthonormal basis \((e_j)\) with \(\sup_j\Delta_x(e_j)\Delta_p(e_j)<\infty\)? The notebook also mentions an unspecified orthogonalization of a critical coherent lattice.
status: As of November 2026, yes for general bases: Meyer wavelets give the product bound and Bourgain gives separate uniform centered second-moment bounds. Balian--Low prohibits the corresponding regular single-window Gabor basis. No assertion covers every ordering or an unspecified Gram--Schmidt procedure.
